pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis secondary to an Ovarian Teratoma THE SMOKING GUN: The characteristic EEG finding of extreme delta brush pattern in a young female with acute psychosis, oro-facial dyskinesias, and autonomic lability, combined with an ultrasound revealing an unsuspected pelvic mass (ovarian teratoma). PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis is a severe autoimmune disorder where autoantibodies (predominantly IgG against the GluN1 subunit of the NMDA receptor) are produced. In many young female patients, ectopic neural tissue contained within an underlying ovarian teratoma triggers this autoimmune response. The antibodies bind to surface NMDA receptors in the brain, causing receptor cross-linking and internalisation. This drop in functional NMDA receptor density leads to a breakdown in synaptic plasticity, triggering a sequential presentation: initial psychiatric symptoms, extrapyramidal movement disorders, autonomic instability, and life-threatening hypoventilation. Treatment requires tumor resection alongside aggressive immunotherapy (plasma exchange, IVIG, steroids, and rituximab).
